title.en: Analytic volume, quadrature estimate and mesh volume compared

summary: Report the analytic volume, the quadrature estimate and the tessellated mesh volume as three separate numbers with their error sources.
objective: Quadrature error follows the declared refinement trend, mesh volume approaches the analytic value from below where containment was verified, and units are cubed length units.
applies_when: A solid is generated from a profile curve and its volume is displayed.
The scene uses numerical quadrature, a tessellated mesh, or both.
The profile can touch or approach the axis of revolution.
intent_signals: the displayed volume does not match the integral
check the mesh resolution against the volume
example_prompts: Check the volume reported for this solid of revolution against the integral.

principles: One solid has three numbers: the analytic volume, the quadrature estimate and the volume of the tessellated mesh. They differ for different reasons and must be reported separately.

A predictable error sign needs containment, not just inscribed cross-sections: radial polygons inscribed in each ring reduce the area, but the axial interpolant can bulge outside the solid. For a convex profile such as radius equal to the square of the position on the unit interval, joining endpoint rings gives a cone of volume pi over three, above the true pi over five. Check containment of the whole piecewise-linear surface before applying any underestimate gate, and otherwise report signed tessellation error.
The profile gives the radius, not the diameter; a factor-of-two radius error appears as a factor of four in volume and is easy to mistake for a deliberate scaling choice.
implementation: Compute the analytic disk-method value for the authored profile where a closed form exists and record it with its units.
Compute the quadrature estimate at several partition counts, for example eight, thirty-two and one hundred twenty-eight slices, recording the error against the analytic value at each.

Compute the mesh volume from the rendered triangles with a signed tetrahedron sum over a closed mesh, record the radial and axial segment counts, and record whether the axial interpolant stays inside the solid for this profile.

Repeat with a profile that reaches zero at an endpoint, where the parameterization degenerates to a single point; whether a surface normal exists there depends on the profile, since a cone apex has none while a spherical pole is smooth, so record which case the fixture is and how per-vertex normals are produced.
observable_checks: Quadrature error follows the refinement trend expected for the declared rule and profile, reported as a series of errors with their partition counts; smoothness alone does not make the error decrease at every individual count, so the trend rather than a per-step decrease is the observable.

Where containment was verified, mesh volume stays below the analytic value and approaches it as segment counts rise; where it was not, the signed difference is reported with its sign explained by the profile shape rather than treated as a defect.
Displayed units are cubed length units consistent with the profile; a radius-versus-diameter mistake shows as a factor of four and is reported as such.

known_limits: Applies to the declared region under a nonnegative profile; regions crossing the axis or containing cavities need a different formulation.
Authored verification guidance; no computation or render was run for this record.
creative_affordances: Adapt the scenario, scale and presentation to your subject; this record fixes what must be checked, not how the scene must look.

claims.statement: For a continuous nonnegative function on a closed interval, revolving the region bounded by its graph and the axis produces a volume equal to pi times the integral of the square of the function over that interval.
claims.scope: The disk method as stated in the cited rule; regions crossing the axis or with cavities require a different rule.
